briefing.opening: Good morning. We will now commence the climate briefing for October 23, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Unprecedented Climate Crisis Strikes the World
sections.content: According to major news released today, the severe impacts of climate change are becoming increasingly prominent worldwide. This past summer, Europe experienced a deadly heatwave, resulting in approximately 50,000 deaths, with two-thirds of these fatalities attributed to climate change [3, 5, 11, 21, 24, 128, 135, 140, 141, 143]. Domestically, the weather front has moved 200km northward, bringing heavy rains and late-season heat, and an analysis indicates an increased compound risk of heavy rainfall and heatwaves on the Korean Peninsula [1, 19, 29]. Furthermore, warnings about the spread of livestock infectious diseases and the fact that 96% of the world's coastal coral reef ecosystems are in a 'critical' state, facing a risk of complete collapse within 50 years, highlight a crisis across entire ecosystems [7, 23]. The UN projects that even if all countries fully implement their current reduction targets, the global average temperature will rise by 2.6 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels by the end of this century. It also pointed out that South Korea, with its current policies, will find it difficult to achieve its Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) for greenhouse gas reduction [127].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Domestic Efforts to Combat Climate Change and Transition to Carbon Neutrality
sections.content: Amidst this crisis, various efforts are underway domestically to address climate change and achieve carbon neutrality. The Korea Meteorological Administration (KMA) plans to strengthen its monitoring of climate change-inducing substances in the Korean Peninsula's interior and expand observations to include aerosols [14, 15], while institutions like the Korea National Arboretum are enhancing cooperation in plant management for climate change response [17]. Notably, designation criteria for 'Just Transition Special Zones' have been established for regions impacted by job losses during the transition to carbon neutrality, demonstrating the government's commitment to minimizing regional damage through employment and business support [31, 39, 43, 49, 62, 72, 78]. Furthermore, citizen-participatory carbon neutrality initiatives, such as Gwangmyeong City's creation of carbon gardens and incentives like 4x carbon neutrality points for using 'Ziku' electric bicycles, are also expanding to encourage everyday carbon-neutral practices [35, 53, 64].

sections.title: 🌱 The Advent of the Renewable Energy Era and its Challenges
sections.content: Today marks a significant day as it is the first commemorative ceremony held since 'Renewable Energy Day' was designated as an official commemorative day [79, 85, 91, 95]. The news that renewable energy installed capacity has surpassed 41GW, exceeding coal-fired power generation capacity for the first time in history, signals an acceleration of the energy transition [81, 97, 99, 113]. Various local governments, including Hwasun County and Hapcheon County, are actively working to expand renewable energy at the local level, securing resident support budgets through competitive renewable energy projects and exploring ways to utilize renewable energy to increase income for residents in water source protection areas [96, 116, 120, 124]. However, challenges remain in the expansion of renewable energy, such as solar power developers protesting against the government on the first 'Renewable Energy Day' [87], and critical perspectives being raised regarding renewable energy subsidies [115].

sections.title: 🌍 Current Status and Key Issues of International Climate Response
sections.content: The international community continues to face pressure and engage in discussions regarding climate change response. The UN Climate Loss and Damage Fund has decided to provide its first support of 26.5 billion KRW for Nepal's 'Great Flood' damage, emphasizing the importance of international assistance for losses and damages caused by climate change [12, 22]. Meanwhile, the UK is experiencing difficulties in disaster response, including deploying military aircraft to suppress wildfires caused by climate change [129], and there have been criticisms that major emitting countries are showing insufficient climate action despite their health-related commitments [142]. Analyses suggesting that the arms race exacerbates the climate crisis, coupled with the increased prominence of the Arctic shipping route due to the Middle East crisis, demonstrate that climate change is not merely an environmental issue but is complexly intertwined with international security and geopolitical concerns [18, 27].

briefing.closing: This concludes today's briefing. In this era of climate crisis, our collective efforts are urgently needed for a sustainable future. This concludes the climate briefing for October 23, 2026.
